title: Hybrid identity: Entra Connect and on-prem Active Directory
summary: Bridge on-premises Active Directory with Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Connect Sync, choosing the right sign-in method and understanding how a device earns a cloud identity through hybrid join. You will learn to operate, monitor and troubleshoot the sync engine like an engineer, not a button-pusher.
objectives: Explain what hybrid identity is and why organisations run on-prem AD alongside Entra ID
Describe the Entra Connect Sync architecture: connector spaces, metaverse and the sync engine
Compare Password Hash Sync, Pass-through Authentication and Federation and choose the right one
Operate the sync scheduler and trigger delta and initial sync cycles from PowerShell
Explain source anchor / immutableID, soft and hard matching, and UPN considerations
Diagnose Entra hybrid join state with dsregcmd and monitor health with Connect Health

quiz.q: In the Entra Connect Sync engine, what is the role of the metaverse?
options: It stores the encrypted password hashes before they leave the server
It is the central aggregated view that joins objects from each connector space before export
It is the staging server's read-only replica of Entra ID
It is the cloud-side directory that Conditional Access reads from
quiz.why: The metaverse is the consolidated in-engine view. Objects flow from each connected directory into its connector space, then inbound sync rules project and join them into the metaverse, and outbound rules export the result to the target connector space.

quiz.q: An organisation needs sign-in to keep working at the cloud even if all on-prem infrastructure is offline, with the lowest operational overhead. Which sign-in method best fits?
quiz.why: Password Hash Sync synchronises a hash-of-the-hash to Entra ID, so authentication happens entirely in the cloud and survives a complete on-prem outage with minimal infrastructure. PTA and AD FS both depend on on-prem components being reachable to validate sign-ins.

quiz.q: Which attribute does Entra Connect use by default as the source anchor (immutableID) for objects synced from on-prem AD?
options: objectGUID converted, with ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid as the modern default
quiz.why: Newer Entra Connect builds use ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid as the source anchor by default (populating it from objectGUID if empty). This makes the anchor writable and portable, which is what allows safe forest migrations and rebuilds without orphaning cloud objects.

quiz.q: A user reports a change made in on-prem AD has not appeared in Entra ID after a few minutes. Which command lets you trigger an immediate incremental synchronisation?
quiz.why: Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta runs an incremental cycle that processes only changes since the last run. Initial (full) reprocesses everything and reimports rules, which is heavier and reserved for rule or configuration changes.

quiz.q: When an on-prem account is matched to an existing cloud account, explain the difference between soft match and hard match.
quiz.answer: Soft match links an on-prem object to a cloud object automatically when their primary SMTP / proxyAddresses or userPrincipalName align, with no manual action. Hard match is when you explicitly set the cloud object's immutableID to equal the Base64 of the on-prem source anchor so the next sync binds them deliberately. Soft match is convenient for clean mail attributes; hard match is the reliable fix when soft match fails or anchors must be repaired.
quiz.why: Both stop the engine creating a duplicate cloud object. Soft match relies on matching mail/UPN attributes; hard match forces the link by aligning the immutableID, and is the controlled tool when soft matching cannot find or trust the attributes.

quiz.q: On a Windows 11 device that should be Entra hybrid joined, dsregcmd /status shows AzureAdJoined : NO and DomainJoined : YES. In one or two sentences, what does this tell you and where would you look first?
quiz.answer: The device is domain-joined to on-prem AD but has not yet completed its cloud registration, so it is not hybrid joined. Check that the SCP (service connection point) points at the right tenant, that the device can reach Entra endpoints, that the computer object is syncing via Entra Connect, and review the Diagnostic Data / dsregcmd /status output and the User State section for join errors.
quiz.why: Hybrid join requires both DomainJoined : YES and AzureAdJoined : YES. AzureAdJoined : NO means the automatic device registration has not succeeded — typically an SCP, connectivity, or sync (the computer object reaching Entra) problem.

body_markdown:
## Why hybrid identity exists

Most enterprises did not start in the cloud. They have years of investment in on-premises **Active Directory** (AD) — group policy, file shares, line-of-business apps that authenticate against domain controllers. They also need Microsoft 365, Intune and Conditional Access, which live in **Microsoft Entra ID**. **Hybrid identity** bridges the two so a user has one identity, one password and one sign-on experience whether they hit an on-prem file share or a cloud app.

The bridge is **Microsoft Entra Connect** (the sync client) running **Entra Connect Sync**. It reads objects from AD, transforms them, and provisions matching objects into Entra ID, keeping them in step.

## The sync engine architecture

The engine is not a simple copy. Each connected directory has a **connector space** — a staging area holding a snapshot of that directory's objects. Inbound sync rules project objects into a central **metaverse**, the consolidated view that joins the on-prem user and the cloud user into one record. Outbound rules then export from the metaverse into the Entra ID connector space.

```text
On-prem AD ──import──> AD connector space
                              │ inbound sync rules
                              ▼
                         METAVERSE  (joined view)
                              │ outbound sync rules
                              ▼
               Entra ID connector space ──export──> Entra ID
```

Understanding this pipeline is what lets you reason about *why* an attribute did or did not flow.

## Choosing a sign-in method

Three options decide where the password is actually validated:

- **Password Hash Sync (PHS)** — a hash of the AD password hash is synced to Entra ID. Authentication happens in the cloud, survives a full on-prem outage, and is the lowest-overhead choice. Recommended default.
- **Pass-through Authentication (PTA)** — the password is validated against on-prem AD in real time by a lightweight agent. No password material in the cloud, but it depends on the agent and DCs being reachable.
- **Federation (AD FS)** — sign-in is redirected to an on-prem federation farm. Most control and most infrastructure; reserve it for specific requirements like third-party MFA or smart-card-only auth.

**Seamless single sign-on (SSO)** can sit on top of PHS or PTA to give Kerberos-style silent sign-in on domain-joined devices.

## The sync cycle and scheduler

By default the scheduler runs a **delta (incremental)** sync every 30 minutes, processing only changes. A full **initial** sync reimports everything and is triggered when you change rules. Operate it from PowerShell on the Connect server:

```powershell
# See the current schedule and whether sync is enabled
Get-ADSyncScheduler

# Force an immediate incremental (delta) run
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta

# Force a full reimport + reprocess (heavier; after rule changes)
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Initial
```

## Anchors, matching and devices

Every object needs a stable **source anchor** (the **immutableID**). Modern Connect uses **ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid**, a writable attribute that makes forest migrations safe. When an on-prem object meets an existing cloud object, the engine performs a **soft match** on mail/UPN attributes; if that fails you perform a **hard match** by setting the cloud object's immutableID to the Base64 of the source anchor. Watch the **UPN**: the on-prem UPN suffix should be a verified domain in the tenant, or users end up with an `.onmicrosoft.com` UPN.

A device gets its cloud identity through **Entra hybrid join**: the domain-joined computer is registered with Entra ID (its object syncs up via Connect), so it appears as a hybrid-joined device and can satisfy Conditional Access. Verify it on the endpoint:

```text
C:\> dsregcmd /status

+----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Device State                                                         |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+
             AzureAdJoined : YES
          EnterpriseJoined : NO
              DomainJoined : YES
               Virtual Desktop : NOT SET
                  DeviceId : 2b8c...e91
```

Both `AzureAdJoined : YES` and `DomainJoined : YES` confirm a successful hybrid join. Use **Entra Connect Health** to monitor sync status, errors and latency, and run a **staging server** — a second Connect instance importing but not exporting — for high availability and safe upgrades.

## Your task

On a test Connect server, run `Get-ADSyncScheduler` and record the current sync interval and whether sync is enabled. Change a user's attribute (e.g. department) in on-prem AD, force a delta cycle with `Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta`, and confirm it lands in Entra ID. Then on a hybrid-joined Windows device run `dsregcmd /status`, capture the Device State and SSO State sections, and write a short note explaining which sign-in method your tenant uses and why it is the correct choice for that environment.

slides.title: Hybrid identity: Entra Connect and on-prem Active Directory
slides.sub: Month 3 - Advanced Endpoint Security & Identity  |  Lesson 5
slides.narration: Welcome back. In this lesson we connect two worlds: your on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID in the cloud. This is hybrid identity, and it's the backbone of nearly every enterprise running Microsoft 365 today. By the end you'll understand the sync engine, you'll be able to choose the right sign-in method, and you'll know how a device earns its cloud identity through hybrid join. We're going to operate this like engineers, not button-pushers.

slides.title: Why hybrid identity exists
bullets: Most enterprises have years of investment in on-prem A D.
They also need Microsoft 365, Intune and Conditional Access.
Hybrid identity gives users one identity and one password.
Entra Connect is the bridge between A D and Entra ID.

They have years of investment in on-prem A D: group policy, file shares, apps that authenticate against domain controllers. But they also need the cloud — Microsoft 365, Intune, Conditional Access — and that lives in Entra ID. Hybrid identity bridges the two so a user has one identity, one password, and one sign-on experience whether they hit a file share or a cloud app. The bridge is Microsoft Entra Connect running Connect Sync.

slides.title: The sync engine architecture
bullets: Each directory has a connector space — a staging snapshot.
Inbound rules project objects into the central metaverse.
The metaverse is the joined view of on-prem and cloud.
Outbound rules export from the metaverse to Entra ID.
slides.code:
On-prem AD --import--> AD connector space
   inbound rules -> METAVERSE (joined view)
   outbound rules -> Entra ID connector space
   --export--> Entra ID
slides.narration: The engine is not a simple copy, and understanding it is what separates a real engineer from a guesser. Each connected directory has a connector space, a staging area holding a snapshot of that directory's objects. Inbound sync rules project those objects into a central metaverse — the consolidated view that joins the on-prem user and the cloud user into one record. Outbound rules then export from the metaverse into the Entra ID connector space, and from there to the cloud. When you can picture this pipeline, you can reason about exactly why an attribute did, or did not, flow.

slides.title: Sign-in method: Password Hash Sync
bullets: A hash of the A D password hash is synced to Entra ID.
Authentication happens entirely in the cloud.
Survives a full on-prem outage, lowest overhead.
Microsoft's recommended default for most tenants.
slides.narration: Now the big decision: where does the password actually get validated? The first option is Password Hash Sync, or P H S. A hash of the A D password hash is synced up to Entra ID, so authentication happens entirely in the cloud. The huge advantage is resilience: if your entire on-prem environment goes dark, cloud sign-in keeps working. It has the lowest operational overhead, and it's Microsoft's recommended default for most tenants. Note it's a hash of a hash — the original password is never sent.

slides.title: PTA and Federation
bullets: Pass-through Auth validates the password against on-prem A D live.
P T A keeps no password material in the cloud.
Federation with A D F S redirects sign-in on-prem.
Federation gives most control but most infrastructure.
slides.narration: The second option is Pass-through Authentication, P T A. A lightweight agent validates the password against on-prem A D in real time, so no password material lives in the cloud — but it depends on that agent and your domain controllers being reachable. The third is Federation with A D F S, where sign-in is redirected to an on-prem federation farm. Federation gives you the most control and demands the most infrastructure, so reserve it for specific needs like a third-party M F A provider or smart-card-only authentication. For most people, P H S wins.

slides.title: Seamless SSO
bullets: Seamless S S O sits on top of P H S or P T A.
Gives Kerberos-style silent sign-in on domain devices.
Users on a corporate device aren't re-prompted.
It is not a sign-in method on its own — an add-on.
slides.narration: On top of either P H S or P T A you can layer Seamless single sign-on, or seamless S S O. This gives a Kerberos-style silent sign-in for users on domain-joined devices on the corporate network — they reach cloud apps without being re-prompted for credentials. The key thing to remember is that seamless S S O is not a sign-in method in its own right; it's an enhancement that rides on P H S or P T A. On modern Entra-joined and hybrid-joined devices, primary refresh tokens often make it redundant, but you'll still meet it in the field.

slides.title: The sync cycle and scheduler
bullets: Default scheduler runs a delta sync every 30 minutes.
Delta processes only changes since the last run.
Initial does a full reimport — used after rule changes.
Get-ADSyncScheduler shows the current configuration.
slides.code:
Get-ADSyncScheduler

# force an incremental run
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta

# full reimport + reprocess
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Initial
slides.narration: By default the scheduler runs a delta, or incremental, sync every thirty minutes, processing only what changed. A full initial sync reimports everything and reprocesses the rules — you trigger that after changing your sync rules. You operate this from PowerShell on the Connect server. Get dash A D Sync Scheduler shows you the current schedule and whether sync is even enabled. Start dash A D Sync Sync Cycle with policy type Delta forces an immediate incremental run — that's the one you'll reach for when a change hasn't appeared yet. Policy type Initial is the heavier full run.

slides.title: Anchors, matching and UPNs
bullets: The source anchor (immutableID) uniquely ties the objects.
Modern Connect uses ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid — writable, portable.
Soft match links on mail/UPN; hard match sets immutableID.
On-prem UPN suffix must be a verified domain in the tenant.
slides.narration: Every object needs a stable source anchor, the immutableID, so the engine always knows the cloud object and the on-prem object are the same thing. Modern Connect uses m s dash D S dash Consistency Guid, a writable attribute that makes forest migrations safe. When an on-prem object meets an existing cloud object, the engine tries a soft match on mail and U P N attributes; if that fails, you perform a hard match by setting the cloud object's immutableID to the Base64 of the source anchor. And watch your U P Ns: the on-prem U P N suffix must be a verified domain in the tenant, or users get stuck with an onmicrosoft dot com U P N.

slides.title: Entra hybrid join and the device
bullets: A domain-joined computer is registered with Entra ID.
Its computer object syncs up via Connect.
The device becomes hybrid joined and can satisfy CA.
dsregcmd /status confirms the join state on the endpoint.
slides.code:
C:\> dsregcmd /status

  AzureAdJoined : YES
   DomainJoined : YES
       DeviceId : 2b8c...e91
slides.narration: So how does a device earn a cloud identity? Through Entra hybrid join. A computer that's domain-joined to on-prem A D is automatically registered with Entra ID — its computer object syncs up through Connect — and it then appears as a hybrid-joined device, which means it can satisfy Conditional Access policies that require a managed device. You verify this right on the endpoint with d s reg c m d slash status. You want to see both Azure A D Joined YES and Domain Joined YES. If Azure A D Joined says NO, the cloud registration hasn't completed — usually a service connection point, connectivity, or sync problem.

slides.title: Health and high availability
bullets: Entra Connect Health monitors sync status and errors.
It surfaces latency, export errors and object failures.
A staging server imports but does not export.
Staging gives high availability and safe upgrades.
slides.narration: Two operational pieces finish the picture. Entra Connect Health gives you cloud-side monitoring of your sync: status, latency, export errors, object-level failures — your early warning system. And for resilience, you run a staging server: a second Connect instance that imports and processes everything but does not export. It's a warm standby you can promote if the primary fails, and it's also how you safely test an upgrade or a rule change before it touches production. No serious hybrid deployment runs a single Connect server with no staging partner.

slides.title: Recap & your task
bullets: Connect Sync joins on-prem A D and Entra ID via the metaverse.
P H S is the resilient default; P T A and Federation cost more.
Operate the scheduler with Get-ADSyncScheduler and delta cycles.
Task: trigger a delta sync and read dsregcmd /status on a device.
slides.narration: Let's recap. Hybrid identity uses Connect Sync to join on-prem A D and Entra ID through connector spaces and the metaverse. Password Hash Sync is the resilient, low-overhead default; Pass-through Auth and Federation buy you specific control at the cost of on-prem dependencies. You operate the engine with Get dash A D Sync Scheduler and force changes through with a delta sync cycle. And a device earns its cloud identity through hybrid join, which you confirm with d s reg c m d slash status. Your task: on a test server run Get dash A D Sync Scheduler and note the interval, change a user attribute in A D, force a delta cycle and confirm it reaches Entra ID. Then run d s reg c m d slash status on a hybrid-joined device, capture the Device State and S S O State sections, and write a short note on which sign-in method your tenant uses and why. See you in the next lesson.
